setlist.title: He Was a Friend of Mine

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Eleven** (5 reviews): Reviewer finds this Eleven pretty good, though not the finest version ever played; Reviewer calls this the hottest Eleven they have heard, with Jerry and Phil relentless throughout [4][5][7][8][10]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Show opens with Lovelight, which takes a while to groove but becomes a great version; Opening Lovelight is full of fire and funk; with a second one it frames a Dark Star sandwich [6][13]
- **Me and My Uncle** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Me and My Uncle that follows the opener gutsy [13]
- **Doin' That Rag** (1 review): Rag follows Me and My Uncle, is played well, and includes some strong jamming [6]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-14.sbd.skinner.5182.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 104 min; rated 4.39/5 by 33 [1]. Said about its sound: On this copy the William Tell section and opening jam sit inside the Saint Stephen track, not The Eleven [5]
- **gd1969-06-14.150775.SBD.DAT.Bear.Latvala.Pollack.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 11 songs; 101 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Cuts in Saint Stephen and Drums match shnid 5182 but are cleaned up and barely noticeable [2]
- **gd1969-06-14.155178.sbd.bear.latvala.pollack.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 9 songs; 103 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Tape flips occur during Saint Stephen and Drums [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer believes they attended, and says the listed venue doesn't exist; likely the gym at Monterey Peninsula College [15]
- Wayne Ceballos of AUM adds vocals [2]
- Wayne Ceballos sings secondary vocals on the second Lovelight; Pigpen plays Hammond B3 and harmonica [3]
- Reviewer thinks the show overall is decent but slightly weak by 1969 standards [5]
- Reviewer finds this Eleven less tight than the version on Live/Dead [8]
- Lovelight bracketing the whole show is rare; reviewer knows no other show that repeats it [10]
- Widely traded show that usually appears in Deadbase's 1969 top ten surveys [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-14.sbd.skinner.5182.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Tiedrich, David Hollister, Jim Skinner; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Normalized in SoundForge, then pitch shifted down 89 cents at highest accuracy [1]
- **gd1969-06-14.150775.SBD.DAT.Bear.Latvala.Pollack.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Recorded by Bear DAT source from Joel Pollack; transferred by Transfer by Charlie Miller Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel October 06, 2020; source: SBD > Bear’s master cassette (Ampex C90) > Dick’s cassette (TDK-SA-X100) > DAT 16bit/48kHz [2]
- **gd1969-06-14.155178.sbd.bear.latvala.pollack.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Joel Pollack; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bear’s Master Soundboard Cassettes (Ampex C90) > Dick Latvala's 1st generation cassettes (Tascam 122mkIII deck)(TDK SA-X 100) > Joel Pollack's DAT (16/48) [3]. Also: Pitch-corrected, level-corrected transfer from Pollack's DAT; not a remaster of shnid 150775, which runs 3.65% fast [3]
